newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Six-month renewal recommended for U.N. Lebanon force.
newsitem.headline: Six-month renewal recommended for U.N. Lebanon force.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan recommended on Friday another six month renewal, until January 31, 1998, of the 4,488-member U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL)
"The level of hostilities in southern Lebanon rose somewhat during the past six months and civilians were again targeted or put at risk," Annan said in a written report to the Security Council.
"The situation remained volatile and continues to give cause for serious concern," he added.

UNIFIL, comprising contingents from Fiji, Finland, France, Ghana, Ireland, Italy, Nepal, Norway and Poland, was established in 1978 to restore the Lebanese government's authority over the southern part of the country after an Israeli incursion against Palestinian guerrillas.

After Israel withdrew its troops following a 1982 invasion, it retained a so-called security zone along the Lebanese side of the border, aided by its allies of the South Lebanon Army militia, to block attacks against northern Israel. This has resulted in frequent clashes mainly with Iranian-backed guerrillas.

Referring to the inability of the U.N. force to deploy up to the international border, the report said although UNIFIL "continued to be prevented from implementing its mandate, its contribution to stability and the protection it is able to afford the population of the area remain important."

"I therefore recommend that the Security Council accede to the request of the government of Lebanon and extend the mandate of UNIFIL for another period of six months, until January 31, 1998," Annan said.

He also drew attention to the force's precarious financial situation, saying unpaid assessments owed by U.N. members for its upkeep amounted to some $176 million, representing money owed to troop-contributing countries. UNIFIL costs about $125 million a year.
